rules.title: New York: New York city time
rules.scope: New York, before standard time

end.note: The city resolved that its time conform to the new standard at noon on 18 November 1883; the Western Union time ball fell at noon Eastern time, and the City Hall clock was stopped at 12:12 city time (12:08:01.62 Eastern) until the new time caught up.

uncertainty.reason: The City Hall clock was stopped for 3 min 58.38 s to change from city time to Eastern time, so city time was 4 h 56 min 1.62 s behind Greenwich.

rules.title: New York: Eastern standard time
rules.scope: New York, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: The city resolved that its time conform to the new standard at noon on 18 November 1883; the Western Union time ball fell at noon Eastern time, and the City Hall clock was stopped at 12:12 city time (12:08:01.62 Eastern) until the new time caught up.

uncertainty.reason: The mayor signed the resolution that from noon on 18 November 1883 all time in the city conform to the 75th-meridian standard.

rules.title: Baltimore: Baltimore city time
rules.scope: Baltimore, before standard time

end.note: Announced for noon on 18 November 1883; whether noon by the old or the new time is not said, and the window covers both.

uncertainty.reason: The change to standard time advanced Baltimore time 6 min 28 s, so city time was 5 h 6 min 28 s behind Greenwich.

rules.title: Baltimore: Eastern standard time
rules.scope: Baltimore, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: Announced for noon on 18 November 1883; whether noon by the old or the new time is not said, and the window covers both.

uncertainty.reason: The new standard was announced to take effect at noon on 18 November 1883, with city time reckoned by it.

rules.title: Washington: Washington mean time
rules.scope: Washington, before standard time

end.note: Noon Eastern time on 18 November 1883, when the railroads and part of the city changed; the offset used here does not change.

uncertainty.reason: The Naval Observatory signalled Eastern noon 8 min 12 s before Washington noon, so Washington time was 5 h 8 min 12 s behind Greenwich.

rules.title: Washington: Washington mean time kept officially while standard time spread
rules.scope: Washington, 18 November 1883 to the act of 13 March 1884

start.note: Noon Eastern time on 18 November 1883, when the railroads and part of the city changed; the offset used here does not change.

end.note: The act took effect on its approval, 13 March 1884; when the departments and the fire bells changed is not recorded here, and the window runs to the end of March.

uncertainty.reason: From 18 November 1883 the railroads and the businesses dealing with them kept Eastern time, while other businesses, the government departments and the fire bells at noon kept Washington time until Congress acted; the atlas gives Washington time.

rules.title: Washington: Eastern standard time
rules.scope: Washington, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: The act took effect on its approval, 13 March 1884; when the departments and the fire bells changed is not recorded here, and the window runs to the end of March.

uncertainty.reason: The act of 13 March 1884 makes the mean time of the 75th meridian the legal standard of time in the District of Columbia.

rules.title: Providence: Providence time (local mean time)
rules.scope: Providence, before standard time

end.note: The city authorities adopted the new time on Tuesday 20 November 1883, two days after the railroads; the hour is not reported, and noon is used.

uncertainty.reason: Providence time is described as about fifteen minutes ahead of the railroads' standard time; the atlas uses the mean time of the city's longitude, 14 min 21 s ahead.

rules.note: Offset computed from the city's longitude, 240 seconds per degree.

rules.title: Providence: Eastern standard time
rules.scope: Providence, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: The city authorities adopted the new time on Tuesday 20 November 1883, two days after the railroads; the hour is not reported, and noon is used.

uncertainty.reason: The city authorities adopted the new time on Tuesday 20 November 1883.

rules.title: Indianapolis: Indianapolis local time (local mean time)
rules.scope: Indianapolis, before standard time

end.note: Central time went into effect at noon on 18 November 1883 and the court-house clock was set back that afternoon; the jewelers were to change their regulators the next day.

uncertainty.reason: Reports give the change as fifteen or sixteen minutes (the court-house clock was set back sixteen); the atlas uses the mean time of the city's longitude, 15 min 22 s ahead of Central time.

rules.note: Offset computed from the city's longitude, 240 seconds per degree.

rules.title: Indianapolis: Central standard time
rules.scope: Indianapolis, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: Central time went into effect at noon on 18 November 1883 and the court-house clock was set back that afternoon; the jewelers were to change their regulators the next day.

uncertainty.reason: Central standard time went into effect at noon on 18 November 1883 and the court-house clock was set back the same afternoon.

rules.title: Louisville: Louisville city time
rules.scope: Louisville, before standard time

end.note: The fire bells rang noon by the new time on 18 November 1883 and the city clock was turned back 18 minutes.

uncertainty.reason: The city clock was turned back 18 minutes to Central time, so city time was 5 h 42 min behind Greenwich (the mean time of the city's longitude would be 16 min 58 s ahead of Central time).

rules.title: Louisville: Central standard time
rules.scope: Louisville, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: The fire bells rang noon by the new time on 18 November 1883 and the city clock was turned back 18 minutes.

uncertainty.reason: The fire bells rang noon by Central time on 18 November 1883 and the city clock was set back to it.

rules.title: Chicago: Chicago time (local mean time)
rules.scope: Chicago, before standard time

end.note: Inaugurated in the city at noon on Sunday 18 November 1883.

uncertainty.reason: Central time is reported as nine minutes slower than Chicago time; the mean time of the city's longitude is 9 min 24 s ahead of Central time.

rules.note: Offset computed from the city's longitude, 240 seconds per degree.

rules.title: Chicago: Central standard time
rules.scope: Chicago, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: Inaugurated in the city at noon on Sunday 18 November 1883.

uncertainty.reason: Standard time was inaugurated in the city at noon on 18 November 1883 and adopted by the railroads, the Board of Trade, hotels and businesses; action by the city government is not reported.

rules.title: Saint Paul: Saint Paul mean time
rules.scope: Saint Paul, before standard time

end.note: At noon on Sunday 25 November 1883, a week after the railroads of the east.

uncertainty.reason: The Globe calls the old time the city's "former meantime", twelve minutes behind the new; the mean time of the city's longitude is 12 min 22 s behind Central time.

rules.note: Offset computed from the city's longitude, 240 seconds per degree.

rules.title: Saint Paul: Central standard time
rules.scope: Saint Paul, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: At noon on Sunday 25 November 1883, a week after the railroads of the east.

uncertainty.reason: Standard time was inaugurated at noon on 25 November 1883, and the city council and chamber of commerce adopted it.

rules.title: Minneapolis: Minneapolis local time (local mean time)
rules.scope: Minneapolis, before standard time

end.note: Generally adopted on 25 November 1883; the hour is not reported, and noon is used, as in Saint Paul.

uncertainty.reason: Assumed to be the mean time of the city's longitude, 13 min 3 s behind Central time, as in neighbouring Saint Paul; no report gives Minneapolis's own figure.

rules.note: Offset computed from the city's longitude, 240 seconds per degree.

rules.title: Minneapolis: Central standard time
rules.scope: Minneapolis, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: Generally adopted on 25 November 1883; the hour is not reported, and noon is used, as in Saint Paul.

uncertainty.reason: The new standard time was to be generally adopted in the city on 25 November 1883.
